independent.summary: Linked documents (LEO-144) are retired as dead pages. A stored document URL appears in NO result list when it is deliberately not re-fetched (`docKnown = storedHashMap` when the linking page's hash is unchanged) or when it is fetched and its text still hashes to the stored hash (embedLinkedDocs `continue`s without pushing to `pages` or `chunks`). Since the rescrape queue is seeded only with `baseUrl`, an off-domain Drive/PDF URL can never be crawled either, so `reachedKeys()` has no evidence for it, `missedCrawls` reaches MAX_MISSES after two rescrapes, and `applyRetirement` deletes the document's ScrapedPage row and all its `scraped` chunks — the brochure's dates/prices leave the corpus until the next run re-fetches them (the row is gone, so `known.has()` is false), producing a permanent delete/re-embed churn cycle.

The 'page went empty → clear its chunks' fix is only reachable inside `if (hasNormalChanges || hasThinChanges)`. A rescrape whose only change is a page that now yields zero chunks (no other page produced a normal chunk and no thin group was rebuilt) skips the whole loop, so the page keeps its stale chunks AND its `contentHash` is never advanced — the same state recurs on every subsequent run, so gap 2 is never fixed for that case.

The MAX_PAGES guard compares `reached.size` — distinct page keys derived from the result, which includes synthetic thin-group URLs, document URLs, robots-disallowed URLs and every `sourceUrls` entry — against the crawl's 500-page fetch cap, not against the crawl's `visited.size`. A crawl that finished comfortably under the cap can therefore exceed 500 derived keys, trip the guard, retire nothing permanently, and log the false reason 'the crawl reached the 500-page cap'.

New deletion path at a group URL that coincides with a page URL. The code just above documents that a canonical group URL can equal a real page's URL ('/staff/'). If that page is in `pageHashUpdates`, is not in `failedUrls`, yields zero chunks this run, and its thin group was NOT rebuilt (no member changed), `clearChunksForUrl` now deletes every `scraped` chunk at that URL — including the still-current group chunk holding the thin members' cards. The previous early return in `replaceChunksForUrl` preserved it.

No credentials or secret handling; the only env vars added are log-level knobs.

Right call — the change adds Chunk and ScrapedPage deleteMany calls (pageRetire.applyRetirement, clearChunksForUrl); the cited line is only the new schema field, but the category judgement is correct.
No external API integration is added or modified; crawl ordering only changes the sequence of fetches the crawler already made.
No CI, deploy, packaging or version config; the new `missedCrawls` field and the two log-level env vars both default safely with no migration step.

summary: The local review reported nothing at all and so missed every defect, including a high-severity data-loss path where linked-document chunks are deleted as 'dead pages' after two rescrapes; its triage answers were all correct but carried only one weak piece of evidence.
